title: Ring formation in bivalent ligand-bivalent receptor aggregation (Posner et al., 1995)
reference: Posner RG, Wofsy C, Goldstein B (1995). The kinetics of bivalent ligand-bivalent receptor aggregation: ring formation and the breakdown of the equivalent site approximation. Math Biosci 126:171-190. doi:10.1016/0025-5564(94)00045-2

koff__FREE.note: bond dissociation, /s; the same constant breaks a chain bond and reopens a ring

kf__FREE.note: capture of a free ligand arm by a free receptor site, /(molecule*s)

kxf__FREE.note: crosslinking of a tethered ligand to a second receptor, /(molecule*s)

jp__FREE.note: ring closure, /s; first order because both ends are already in one complex, and the only parameter in the collection that acts on aggregate topology rather than on a bond count

notes: The collection's only problem whose aggregates are not trees. Every other aggregation problem here blocks same-complex binding and so forbids cycles; this one adds an explicit ring-closure step, which is the mechanism the paper's title is about and the reason the equivalent-site approximation fails. That gives it a parameter unlike any other in the collection: jp is first order, acts on topology rather than on a bond count, and is visible almost entirely through one observable, the cyclic-dimer population. The other three constants it shares in form with Dembo_JImmunol1978 and Yang_PhysRevE2008, which is deliberate -- the three problems differ in exactly one structural feature each, so a method's results across them say which feature it is sensitive to. The window is the first 100 s of the published 3,000 s protocol: that is where the cyclic-dimer population is still forming, and a trajectory past it costs several times more for a flat mean.
